samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order in which numbers are added can affect the result due to rounding errors. Different groupings of additions may lead to different intermediate sums, which, when rounded at each step, yield distinct final results. This behavior contrasts with exact arithmetic, where the order of addition does not affect the outcome.

Floating-point addition is not associative because the precision of floating-point numbers limits the exactness of calculations. Different order of addition can lead to different rounding errors. This means that \((a + b) + c\) can yield a different result than \(a + (b + c)\) due to these rounding discrepancies.
